name: Blackberry Farm
positioning: Relais & Châteaux resort on a hillside in Walland, Tennessee, in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains, next door to Great Smoky Mountains National Park
best_for: Families wanting guided Smokies adventure programs, ceramics and painting classes and Camp Blackberry
Hikers and bikers who want a trail network and a quieter edge of Great Smoky Mountains National Park next door

facts.text: Blackberry Farm is a Relais & Châteaux resort in Walland, Tennessee, in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains.
Blackberry Farm was named a MICHELIN Two-Key destination in 2026.
Accommodations include Historic Rooms, Estate Rooms, Cottage Suites, Hill Cottages and multi-bedroom houses, all furnished with fine antiques and art.
The interiors are designed by Blackberry Farm Design.
Blackberry Farm sits on a hillside.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, the Farm was built in 1940, and Sandy and Kreis Beall opened it as an intimate country inn in 1976.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, Blackberry Farm is less than half an hour from Knoxville's McGhee Tyson Airport.
Condé Nast Traveler describes the room aesthetic as rustic country chic mixed with bright, functional modernity, with floral wallpaper prints, stone chimneys and overstuffed sofas.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, the Barn restaurant is a timber-frame structure the Bealls moved piece by piece from Pennsylvania Dutch country.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, the Wellhouse spa has a little cafe for tonics and juices to take out to the pool, and it hosts the Farm's yoga and movement classes.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, half of the Farm's 4,200 acres is in conservation.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, the property has a network of hiking and biking trails.

highlights.text: According to Condé Nast Traveler, Blackberry Farm breeds Lagotto Romagnolos, Italian water dogs used to hunt truffles, and guests can visit the kennels.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, Great Smoky Mountains National Park is the Farm's next-door neighbor, and the park's western end is a lot quieter.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, families have guided adventure programs in the Smokies, ceramics and painting classes, and Camp Blackberry for children.
Blackberry Farm brings together wellness, culinary, outdoor adventure and hospitality experiences.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, Blackberry Farm offers intimate live music performances featuring some of the biggest names in the South.

considerations.text: Traditional rates are based on double occupancy and include dinner on the day of arrival through breakfast on the day of departure in the resort's restaurants during traditional meal hours.
Condé Nast Traveler advises guests to plan to dress for dinner.
WhataHotel notes that pricing reflects the resort's ultra-luxury positioning.
